title: Short Stuff: Streisand Effect
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Streisand effect, the phenomenon where attempts to censor or suppress information online backfire and draw more attention to it. The hosts recount Barbra Streisand's 2003 lawsuit against photographer Kenneth Adelman over an aerial coastline erosion photo showing her Malibu home, which led to a surge in downloads; blogger Mike Masnick coined the term on Techdirt. They discuss China's attempt to block Facebook and Twitter driving VPN downloads, the McLibel case against McDonald's, Martha Payne's school lunch blog in Scotland, a Georgia high school girl suspended over a photo of unmasked classmates, and researchers Sue Curry Jensen and Brian Martin's work on outrage management tactics, illustrated with Nazi concealment of the disability euthanasia program. They close with the Fox News lawsuit over 'fair and balanced' against Al Franken's book and a plug for the hosts' book.
topics: Streisand effect China Facebook Twitter VPN
Al Franken Lies and the Lying Liars
Fox News fair and balanced trademark lawsuit

segments.title: Introduction and origin of the Streisand effect
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Streisand effect as the backfire of online censorship, then begin describing Barbra Streisand's attempt to censor a photo before cutting the background and moving on.

segments.title: Streisand's 2003 lawsuit over the Malibu photo
segments.summary: Streisand sued photographer Kenneth Adelman for fifty million dollars over an aerial erosion-project photo showing her Malibu home. The photo's downloads jumped from about six to thousands, and Mike Masnick of Techdirt coined the term Streisand effect.

segments.title: Name popularity and Christmas banter
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why the term caught on, with a tangent about Streisand's music and her jingle bells version.

segments.title: China blocking social media and forbidden fruit
segments.summary: A 2018 study found China's attempt to block Facebook and Twitter led millions to download VPN software. The hosts link this to the forbidden fruit effect.

segments.title: Parenting and the Streisand effect
segments.summary: The hosts compare the Streisand effect to parents trying to hide or downplay things from children.

segments.title: McLibel, Martha Payne and other backfires
segments.summary: Examples include McDonald's suing London Greenpeace volunteers over the McLibel pamphlet, the longest civil trial in British history, and the school board banning Scottish schoolgirl Martha Payne from photographing her lunches after Jamie Oliver tweeted about her blog. A recent Georgia case of a high school girl suspended over a photo of unmasked classmates is also mentioned.

segments.title: Outrage management and Nazi concealment
segments.summary: Researchers Sue Curry Jensen and Brian Martin describe outrage management, a playbook for containing backlash to censorship. They illustrate it with the Nazi concealment of the disability euthanasia program, which used five methods including hiding the program and lying about deaths.

segments.title: Al Franken and Fox News trademark suit
segments.summary: Fox News sued Al Franken over the phrase fair and balanced in his book Lies and the Lying Liars. The judge ruled they were common words, and the lawsuit boosted the book's sales. The hosts joke about their own book title.
topics: Fox News fair and balanced lawsuit

segments.title: Sign-off and book plug
segments.summary: The hosts plug their book and the show's podcast feed and sign off.
